detail.longDescription: I'm building a Selenium based runner where non-technical users compose their own tests. Since the tests may target different web applications, I can't really rely on app specific assertions after a click. Also the user may not see themselve that they have to wait to click a specific web-element and i cannot add a generic wait before everyclick because some test then could take way to long. Is there any generic and reliable way to verify that a Click actually had any effect on the page rather than simply firing on an element that wasnt ready yet e.g., because its event handlers were attached later? I'd like to automatically retry the click if it appears that nothing happened as a result of the first one. But i need to make sure the click result wont happen twice. Currently we just call click() on the WebElement and if no Exception is thrown from selenium we say it was successfull. But in some cases the click just did nothing, which lead to failures ahead.
